class.name: NNBTRoot
class.brief_description: The main node for the Noodle Nodes Behaviour Tree nodes.
class.description: This is the main node for the Noodle Nodes Behaviour Tree nodes. The root node is ticked to update the state of the behaviour tree. The root must have exactly one enabled behaviour tree child. It ticks the first enabled child and returns that child's result. Any further enabled behaviour tree children are ignored; the first time the root is ticked with more than one enabled behaviour tree child it reports a one-time error. The editor shows a configuration warning for the same configuration. [NNSensors] child nodes are allowed in addition to the single behaviour tree child. Sensors do not count as behaviour tree children. If no behaviour tree child is enabled, or the root has no children at all, [method tick] returns [code]FAILURE[/code]. [member blackboard] is the explicitly assigned [NNBlackboard], and an explicit assignment always wins. When it is null the root inherits the effective board of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system, and falls back to its own private per-instance board only when it has no root ancestor. Every root resolves its board from its current position in the scene tree, so reparenting re-resolves it. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and returns to inherited resolution. The private board is never a property, so it is never serialised. Blackboards default to [code]resource_local_to_scene = true[/code], so a board assigned in the inspector is duplicated per scene instance unless you deliberately untick that to share one board. [member actor] is the explicitly assigned actor or [code]null[/code]. [member actor] does not store a resolved fallback; read the resolved actor with [method get_actor], which resolves on demand: the live explicit actor wins, then the node at [member actor_node_path], then the actor of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system, then the root's parent. Because resolution is computed on demand, entering the tree or reparenting re-resolves naturally, and a freed explicit actor falls through to the path, the inherited actor or the parent. Disabling the root interrupts its active run and resets the whole tree, so re-enabling it starts a fresh run on the next tick. Every explicit reset of the root interrupts the active subtree as well. Changing the root's children does not reset the tree: adding or removing a sensor or a non-behaviour-tree node only refreshes the cached sensor list and leaves the active run untouched. When a child order change makes a different enabled behaviour-tree child the one the root ticks, for example because the running child was removed or a new enabled child was inserted before it, the abandoned run is interrupted and the tree resets. Automatic ticking is on by default: while the root is in the tree and enabled, the SceneTree's [code]process_frame[/code] or [code]physics_frame[/code] signal selected by [member process_thread] ticks the tree. The root does not override or disable this node's own [code]_process[/code]/[code]_physics_process[/code], so a script attached to the root keeps its own callbacks and cannot shadow automatic ticking. Connections exist only while the root is in the tree with [member is_enabled] true and a [member process_thread] other than [constant MANUAL], and no tick happens while the root cannot process (paused or process mode disabled). [constant MANUAL] connects neither signal, so a custom scheduler calls [method tick] itself. [member tick_rate] counts eligible frame signal emissions, starting with the first one. A rate of 2 ticks on emissions 1, 3, 5 and so on. The schedule counts emissions, not time, but each tick receives the delta accumulated since the previous tick. Re-arming the schedule (changing [member tick_rate], [member process_thread] or [member is_enabled], entering or leaving the tree, or resetting the tree) restarts the count and discards any accumulated delta, so the next eligible emission is due. The root can be hosted. A host is an ancestor state ([NNSTTickedNodes]) that is active, an ancestor agent action ([NNAction]) that is the agent's current action, or an ancestor HTN task ([NNHTNTask]) whose step is running, and the nearest host ancestor is the one that drives the root. A root nested inside another root's subtree is not hosted across that root; the nearest ancestor root owns its subtree. A host starts the root when it activates, ticks it with the host's own delta on the host's schedule, and interrupts and resets it when it deactivates. A hosted root never ticks from the SceneTree frame signals and never enters anything on [constant NOTIFICATION_READY], because a behaviour tree has no separate enter step: the first host tick starts the run. The host owns the timing, so the root's [member process_thread] and [member tick_rate] are ignored and the editor shows a configuration warning when either would be. [signal finished] is emitted for every run that ends, whether the root is hosted, ticked automatically or ticked by hand. Disabling resets the tree, so enabling starts a fresh run. [signal tree_enabled] and [signal tree_disabled] are emitted only on a real transition of [member is_enabled], never when the root merely leaves the tree. [method get_running_action] returns the deepest node on the active path after the last tick, or [code]null[/code] when nothing is active. When parallel nodes have several active children, the first active child in child order wins. The node is stored as an object ID, so if the active node was freed the method returns [code]null[/code] and never returns a freed object.

constants.constant: The root is ticked automatically from the SceneTree's [code]process_frame[/code] signal.
The root is ticked automatically from the SceneTree's [code]physics_frame[/code] signal. This is the default.
Neither signal is connected and the root never ticks automatically, so a custom scheduler calls [method tick] or [method auto_tick_step] itself.

method.name: auto_tick_step
method.description: The shared body of the frame-signal handlers, and the deterministic driver for custom schedulers. Ticks the tree when the call is due, and returns [code]true[/code] only when it actually ticked. The tick receives the [param delta] plus the deltas of the non-due calls since the previous tick, so it measures the elapsed time rather than one frame's worth. The call is ignored, returning [code]false[/code], when [param process_thread] is not the selected [member process_thread], when the selected thread is [constant MANUAL], when the root is disabled, in the editor, or when [member tick_rate] makes this invocation not due. An ignored call does not advance the [member tick_rate] schedule. This method also works outside the tree, so tests and custom schedulers can drive the schedule deterministically without frame signals.

method.name: get_elapsed_time
method.description: Returns the total [code]delta[/code] this tree has been ticked with since it was created, in seconds. It advances only while the tree is actually ticked, so a paused, disabled or editor-inspected root does not advance it, and it is never reset, not even by [method NNBTNodes.reset]. Nodes that measure durations in tree time, such as [NNBTCooldown], read this clock.

method.name: get_running_action
method.description: Returns the deepest node on the active path after the last tick, or [code]null[/code] when nothing is active. The active path follows the enabled children that the last tick left running: every node on it is enabled, has an active run and has a tick result of [code]RUNNING[/code]. When a parallel node has several active children, the first active child in child order wins. The node is tracked through an object ID, so the method returns [code]null[/code] when the active node was freed and never returns a freed object.

method.name: tick
method.description: This is the behaviour tree tick-method you should be using to tick the tree. It ticks the tree for the given [param delta]. The tree and its nodes read and write their data through the root's effective [NNBlackboard], which every [NoodleNodes] node reaches with the blackboard helpers. The root's actor is its parent unless [member actor] or [member actor_node_path] says otherwise, or an ancestor root provides one; read it with [method NoodleNodes.get_actor]. Manual ticking keeps working while automatic ticking is on, so a script may call this method and also let the automatic callback tick the tree.

members.member: The explicitly assigned actor, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned or the assigned actor was freed. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment. No resolved fallback is ever stored here. To read the resolved actor use [method get_actor], which resolves the explicit actor, then [member actor_node_path], then the actor of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system, then the root's parent on demand.
Fallback actor path, used when no live explicit [member actor] is set. The path is resolved relative to this root and wins over the actor inherited from an ancestor root.

The explicitly assigned typed behaviour tree blackboard resource, or [code]null[/code] when none is assigned. An explicit assignment always wins. When it is [code]null[/code] the root inherits the effective board of the nearest ancestor root of any Noodle Nodes system and uses its own private per-instance board only when it has no root ancestor, so the blackboard helpers work without any setup. Assigning [code]null[/code] clears the assignment and returns to inherited resolution. The private board is never a property, so it is never serialised. Blackboards default to [code]resource_local_to_scene = true[/code], so an assigned inspector board is per scene instance unless you deliberately untick it to share one board. This property is the assignment only; [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard_resource] returns the effective board.

Selects the SceneTree frame signal that drives automatic ticking, not this node's processing flags. Defaults to [constant PHYSICS], so a root auto-ticks once added to a scene. [constant IDLE] uses [code]process_frame[/code], [constant PHYSICS] uses [code]physics_frame[/code] and [constant MANUAL] connects neither so a custom scheduler ticks the tree. Exactly one signal is connected at a time. Out-of-range values fall back to [constant PHYSICS]. Setting this property re-arms the [member tick_rate] schedule. Ignored while an ancestor state or agent action hosts the root, because the host drives every tick; the editor reports a configuration warning when the value would be ignored.

The number of eligible frame signal emissions between automatic ticks. The default of [code]1[/code] ticks every eligible emission, and a rate of 2 ticks on emissions 1, 3, 5 and so on. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Ineligible emissions, such as those for a signal that is not selected, do not advance the count. A tick receives the delta accumulated over the emissions since the previous tick, so the tree measures the same elapsed time whatever the rate. Setting this property or [member process_thread], an [member is_enabled] change, entering or leaving the tree, and a reset re-arm the schedule and discard the accumulated delta. The rate gates the whole tick, including running actions, so it stays at [code]1[/code] by default; [NNAgent] defaults to [code]6[/code] because its rate only throttles thinking. Ignored while an ancestor state or agent action hosts the root, and the editor reports a configuration warning when the value would be ignored.
Microseconds the latest [method tick] call took. Only available in debug builds, and overwritten on each tick.

signal.name: finished
signal.description: Emitted when a tick ends a run with [code]SUCCESS[/code] or [code]FAILURE[/code], with [param succeeded] set to [code]true[/code] for [code]SUCCESS[/code]. Emitted once per finished run, and never for a tick that leaves the tree running. Being hosted, ticked automatically or ticked by hand makes no difference.

signal.name: tree_disabled
signal.description: Emitted when the root is disabled through [member is_enabled], after the tree was reset and the frame-signal connections were updated. Emitted only on a real transition, so disabling an already disabled root does not emit again.

signal.name: tree_enabled
signal.description: Emitted when the root is re-enabled through [member is_enabled], after the whole tree was reset, so the next tick starts a fresh run. Emitted only on a real transition, so enabling an already enabled root does not emit again.
